title: Apex admin conductor and policy linter
creator: Aisha Kapoor
description:
Summary: Build an "apex" Admin Conductor service that compiles human-authored runbooks/playflows into verifiable task graphs, enforces organization policies via a pluggable policy linter, and provides a safe dry-run + sandbox execution path for support automation.

Background: Our current runbooks-as-tasks tooling covers basic templating and execution, but teams still hand-roll safety checks, and support engineers frequently request a faster way to validate flows against org policies (RBAC, secrets usage, escalation windows) before running in production. This project targets developer and on-call productivity improvements while reducing risky manual steps.

Scope:
- Compiler that parses the playflow DSL (YAML/DSL) and emits an idempotent task graph with explicit inputs/outputs and side-effect annotations.
- Policy linter subsystem with rule registry (security, infra-cost, escalation, data residency) and an infra-safe feedback format for UI highlighting.
- Dry-run executor that simulates side effects and integrates with the existing admin sandbox for replayable checks.
- Integration points: Console (preview + lint panel), ops CLI (opsctl apex-validate), and the runbooks task runner (for gated execution).
- Telemetry and tracing to attribute lint failures and runtime deviations to authors and commits.

Deliverables:
- RFC + prototype (parser + two sample policy rules) for review.
- End-to-end demo: compile -> lint -> dry-run -> gated rollout.
- Migration guidance for 3 pilot teams (Support, SRE, Customer Success).

Acceptance criteria:
1) Compiler accepts existing runbook primitives and produces deterministic task graphs with metadata annotations.
2) Linter runs in <500ms for a 20-step playflow and returns actionable diagnostics.
3) Dry-run produces a trace log that maps 1:1 to a real execution trace (where applicable) and flags non-deterministic steps.
4) Console shows lint warnings inline and blocks canary/rollout if critical rules fail.
5) Integration tests and two pilot migrations completed.

Technical approach:
- Reuse the runlet step schema from ops-playflow as the compilation IR. Add an explicit SideEffect enum so the runtime can short-circuit in dry-run mode.
- Linter implemented as WASM-hosted policy plugins to allow rapid rule updates without service restarts; rules written in Rego or JS adapters.
- Dry-run shim in the task runner that substitutes network/infra calls with mocks and records resource intents.
- Add a lint cache keyed by (repo@sha, playflow-hash, policy-set) to accelerate CI checks.

Trade-offs & open questions:
- WASM rule execution increases complexity but improves safety/isolation; alternative is server-side rule interpreter (simpler).
- Level of strictness for blocking rules vs warnings; propose default rules be warning-level and opt-in critical enforcement via project config.
- How to represent secrets use in a way that doesn't leak sensitive info to lint endpoints; propose a secrets-usage tokenization scheme.

Rollout plan:
1) RFC + prototype (week 1-2) -> runbook authors and SRE review.
2) Implement core compiler + linter (week 3-6).
3) Pilot with Support and SRE (week 7-8) - collect usability feedback and add 5 blocking rules.
4) Console integration and release gating (week 9).

Telemetry & Observability:
- Lint telemetry: number of warnings/errors per playflow, top failing rules, rule hit rates.
- Dry-run vs live-exec divergence metric.
- Trace links: playflow -> compile-sha -> run-id.

Safety & Security:
- All lint rule evaluations run in sandboxed WASM with disabled host calls.
- Dry-run logs redact secrets and use ephemeral tokens for external service stubs.
- Security review required before pilot.

Notes/links:
- Design draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/OPS/Apex+Admin+Conductor+Draft
- Prototype repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/ops-apex-prototype
- Related: ENG-314159 (chronos scheduler integration), ENG-672401 (admin-proxy for guarded-runbook-execution)
